final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger between UBS and Credit Suisse over the weekend, with substantial government loss guarantees (CHF 25-50bn), AT1 write-down to zero, and announcement before Asian markets open Sunday evening. Temporary nationalization held as fallback if UBS negotiations fail.
minority_objections: AT1 bondholders will argue this is not a contractual viability event and threaten litigation
Political criticism anticipated regarding UBS monopoly and taxpayer risk exposure
key_conflicts: UBS leverage vs government fiscal constraints: UBS demands full indemnity on CHF 100bn+ assets while government must minimize taxpayer cost
AT1 bondholder treatment vs capital hierarchy: writing down AT1 before full equity wipeout violates traditional creditor hierarchy
Speed vs due diligence: emergency timeline forces acceptance of risks that would normally require weeks of analysis
key_concessions: Federal Council accepts CHF 25-50bn loss guarantees and political cost of reinforcing 'too big to fail'
UBS accepts nominal purchase price (CHF 0.50-1.00/share) and CHF 5-7bn integration costs
FINMA accepts competition law override and writes down AT1 despite anticipated litigation
SNB provides CHF 100bn+ emergency liquidity and accepts some exposure may become fiscal
red_lines: Cannot allow Monday market opening without resolution (FINMA, Federal Council, SNB)
UBS will not accept material risk to its own stability without full government indemnity
SNB will not allow disorderly collapse
Must announce deal with full legal certainty by 20:00 CET Sunday (before 21:00 Asia open)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Integration execution risk of merging two large institutions at emergency speed with only weekend due diligence
Potential for wealth client flight to continue even after merger announcement if confidence not restored
Cross-border resolution complexity dismissed as 'manageable through weekend calls' without detailed planning
Long-term competitive implications of creating a Swiss banking monopoly
downstream_risk_variables: UBS's actual willingness to proceed given 'immense leverage' and ability to make 'impossible demands'
Adequacy of CHF 100bn+ SNB liquidity to prevent weekend collapse before deal closes
Political acceptability threshold for government guarantees if UBS demands exceed CHF 50bn
International regulatory coordination success within 48-hour window
Effectiveness of communication blackout in preventing panic amplification
uncertainty_notes: The room acknowledged 20% probability UBS demands become politically impossible, forcing nationalization pivot. The 5% tail risk of disorderly collapse if weekend bank run exceeds SNB liquidity capacity remained unmitigated. AT1 bondholder litigation outcome uncertain but deemed acceptable trade-off. Actual government guarantee amount (CHF 25-50bn range) left to Saturday negotiations.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Opening rationale states 'Standalone stabilization is not credible. Even with SNB liquidity backstop (announced March 15), client confidence is broken' — drove rejection of liquidity-only path
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Primary recommendation is 'Forced Merger with UBS over the Weekend' with detailed negotiation timeline — the entire decision structure built around this path
marker_evidence.government_support: Government loss guarantees CHF 25-50bn specified as necessary deal term; Federal Council must 'Provide CHF 25-50bn loss guarantees to UBS' listed as likely concession — binding constraint on deal structure
marker_evidence.client_flight: Listed as Decisive Risk A 'Weekend Bank Run Acceleration' that 'Could render Credit Suisse insolvent in liquidity terms before any deal closes' — drove SNB unlimited liquidity requirement and communication blackout
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: FINMA decision to 'write down AT1 bonds to zero (absorb ~CHF 16bn losses)' specified in Saturday and Sunday timelines as necessary action to 'make deal math work for UBS' — concrete decision driven by this risk
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Acknowledged under AT1 section: 'AT1 holders will argue equity should be wiped first, but FINMA will prioritize deal completion over capital hierarchy purity' — noted but explicitly deprioritized, did not change the write-down decision
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 bondholder lawsuits anticipated and prepared for ('will be filed Monday') but dismissed as manageable: 'Will trigger lawsuits, but manageable post-crisis' and 'Not decisive because legal authority exists' — acknowledged but set aside
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Hard deadline 'Monday Asia Market Open (21:00 CET Sunday)' listed as Decisive Risk C; entire timeline structured backward from Sunday 20:00 announcement requirement — forced emergency powers, competition law override, and weekend negotiation compression
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Decisive Risk C states 'Any uncertainty at Asia open = global contagion' and 'Deal must be announced with full legal certainty by 20:00 CET Sunday latest' — this timing constraint shaped every decision milestone and drove the 'no uncertainty' requirement
